answer: Require each agent to post a bond that is locked before it can claim rewards, then slash that bond when a randomly sampled task fails an audit. A pulse of audits can follow a vine of referrals back to its root, so splitting one operator across many identities does not multiply trust: all linked claims expose the same stake to loss. Set the bond above the expected gain from cheap spam, and a knoll of throwaway accounts becomes costly: the attacker must tie up real capital and risk losing it for every identity.
